_comment: Each entry names a registered datrix.languages target, a documented
construct kind (endpoint, entity, field, enum_value, struct_field,
function), and a surface (published, source) whose emitted artifact does
not yet carry the author's DSL comment text -- with a written reason.
pinned_count is the reviewed count of len(exemptions); a realization
change removes its own entry and decrements this field in the SAME
change -- the field never silently drifts from the live count (the gate
fails loud if it does, and fails loud the other way too if an exempted
cell starts passing without its entry being removed -- a stale exemption).

exemptions.reason: No target defines a published landing site for entity-level documentation (architecture-overview.md Decision 39's per-target table specifies published surfaces only for endpoint summary/description and field description). A published entity comment is deliberately dropped rather than promoted onto an invented surface no other target realizes; the entity's own SOURCE-channel comment still reaches a plain comment above its schema classes. Verified against generated output: the fixture's `schemas/catalog_db/product.py` and `models/catalog_db/product.py` carry only synthesized docstrings (`"""Product schemas."""`, `"""Product ORM model."""`); the authored entity comment text is absent.

No target defines a published landing site for entity-level documentation (see the python entry's identical reason). java's JPA @Entity model and DTO records carry only a synthesized Javadoc header; an authored published entity comment is not promoted onto @Schema (a field-only annotation) or any other invented surface. Verified against generated output: the fixture's `model/catalog_db/Product.java` and `dto/catalog_db/ProductCreateRequest.java` class-level Javadoc reads only "Product JPA entity."/"Product create-request DTO." plus the boilerplate auto-generated notice; the authored entity comment text is absent even though this gate now reads `/** ... */` doc blocks structurally.

No target defines a published landing site for entity-level documentation (see the python entry's identical reason). dotnet's POCO model and DTO records carry only a boilerplate `//` header; a published entity comment is not promoted onto an invented `/// <summary>` class-level surface no other target realizes. Verified against generated output: the fixture's `Models/CatalogDb/Product.cs` and `Dtos/CatalogDb/Product.cs` carry only a `//` boilerplate header comment, never a class-level `/// <summary>`; the authored entity comment text is absent.
